industry: Automotive: repair/service shops, collision/hail/glass, detailing, and dealerships (sales + service)
words_and_claims_to_avoid: Dealer: advertised price that excludes mandatory dealer fees, add-ons, reconditioning or 'market adjustment'; rebates the buyer can't get; prices requiring dealer financing or a down payment not stated; vehicles you don't have (FTC Sec. 5; Leader Automotive; March 2026 warning letters; CA SB 766; CA VEH 11713.1).
'$500 OFF any vehicle on the lot' (gold 020) without conditions stated clearly next to it; '$X below MSRP' without the MSRP basis.
Credit trigger terms ('$0 down', '$299/month', '72 months', finance charge) without the Reg Z disclosures: down payment, repayment terms, APR (1026.24(d)).
Lease payments or 'due at signing' without Reg M disclosures: it's a lease, total due at signing, number/amount/timing of payments, security deposit, end-of-term charges (1013.7).
Bait pricing: advertising a car or service you don't intend to sell at that price (16 CFR 238).

'We'll pay your deductible', 'deductible assistance', 'save $500 off your deductible' (gold 016/029) - illegal in Texas for auto claims (Class B misdemeanor, Bus. & Com. Code via HB 1656, 2023) and flagged as possible fraud by Colorado DOI (2025).
'Dealer-only service keeps your warranty' style claims (false under Magnuson-Moss) - and the reverse overclaim 'never any warranty issues' for a shop.
Recall- or DMV-styled 'NOTICE' mail from a private shop (39 USC 3001(h); state law) - the NHTSA letterhead lift (MMR-683) is not available to private businesses.
'Free' inspections that require a purchase or come with undisclosed fees (16 CFR 251); low price ads without likely extra parts/labor disclosed (CA BAR rules).
compliance_notes: FTC CARS Rule: vacated by the 5th Circuit on Jan 27 2025 (NADA v. FTC) on procedural grounds. FTC Section 5 still applies: Leader Automotive/AutoCanada $20M (stipulated order Jan 2025) for bait advertising and junk fees; March 2026 warning letters to 97 dealer groups said advertised prices must be the total price including mandatory dealer fees (excluding government charges), and flagged unavailable rebates, required down payments, financing conditions, undisclosed add-ons and nonexistent vehicles.

California CARS Act (SB 766), operative Oct 1 2026: total price clearly disclosed in any ad for a specific vehicle or financing term and in the first written communication; 2-year record retention including ads.

California VEH 11713.1: specific-vehicle ads identify model, year and license number or VIN portion (stock number alone not enough); price includes all costs except taxes, registration, tire fee, emission charges, finance charges and document/electronic registration fees, with the statutory 'plus government fees and taxes...' language; doc fees can't be called government fees.
Reg Z 12 CFR 1026.24 for credit ads (trigger terms -> down payment, terms, APR). Reg M 12 CFR 1013.7 for lease ads.

Auto repair: California BAR requires firm name, ARD registration number and phone in internet advertising since Oct 1 2025; price ads must disclose likely additional parts/labor. Other states: check repair-shop registration and estimate laws.

Deductible waivers/rebates: Texas HB 1656 (eff. Sept 1 2023) extended the ban to auto insurance; Colorado DOI bulletin (Oct 2025) warns it may be fraud. Check every state before any deductible language.
Magnuson-Moss: manufacturers can't condition warranty on dealer service (unless free); honest 'warranty-safe' messaging is lawful.
Mail lists: DMV-derived data requires express consent for marketing (DPPA 18 USC 2721(b)(12)); use customer DMS data and lawful compiled lists.
Testimonials/reviews genuine and typical (16 CFR 255); FTC also cited bogus reviews in Leader Automotive.
standing_rules: Emotion-agnostic: fear, joy, pride, status, relief, nostalgia are all options; the client chooses.
Every angle and combo carries a sell-the-outcome line.
Unverified (agency/vendor-only) results are labeled; never quote them as fact on a card.
No age/demographic angle unless a cited source supports it for this industry; even then, check Fair Housing / ECOA before using it in housing or credit.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Gold hail cards 'Save up to $500 OFF your deductible' / 'deductible assistance' (016, 029) vs Texas HB 1656 and Colorado DOI bulletin
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law wins: no deductible language; offer claim help, speed and a written warranty.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Gold 020 '$500 OFF any vehicle on the lot' and 'starting at' prices vs FTC Sec. 5 enforcement (Leader Automotive; 2026 warning letters) and CA SB 766
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law wins: total price for specific vehicles; conditions next to any discount.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: CARS Rule vacated (some read it as 'rules relaxed') vs FTC warning letters and California CARS Act
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law wins: the FTC still enforces total-price advertising under Section 5, and California codified it from Oct 1 2026.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: NHTSA DMV-letterhead recall letters lifted repairs 161-348% (MMR-683, official) vs 39 USC 3001(h) / state law for private mail
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Law wins: private shops can't use government letterhead; borrow the plain, specific, personal format only.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Gold 012 stranded-woman roadside fear image vs C-3PO stereotype/anti-pattern notes and EPPM
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Verified fear research + design notes win over the gold example: keep the breakdown fear, show the fix (technician + owner), avoid stereotyped helplessness.
